title: What is Kubernetes? 🤔
description: Discover the problem Kubernetes solves and how it orchestrates containers.

slides.title: Welcome to Progly! 🎉
slides.content:
# You’re about to master Kubernetes

Kubernetes (often called **K8s**) is the world’s most popular container orchestration platform.

By the end of this course, you’ll be able to:
- Run resilient, scalable applications
- Manage clusters like a pro
- Deploy real‑world projects confidently

slides.title: The Problem Before Kubernetes 🐒
slides.content:
## From Monoliths to Microservices

Before containers, apps were deployed on bare‑metal or VMs. Scaling was hard, dependencies clashed, and moving between environments broke things.

Containers (like Docker) fixed packaging, but we still needed to:
- **Run hundreds of containers** across many machines
- **Restart failed ones** automatically
- **Scale up/down** on demand
- **Connect them** with networking and storage

quizData.question: What problem does Kubernetes primarily solve?
quizData.explanation: Kubernetes orchestrates containers—scheduling, scaling, healing, and networking them across a cluster.

slides.title: Container Orchestration Explained 🎻
slides.content:
## Think of an Orchestra Conductor

- **Musicians** = your containers (each plays a part)
- **Conductor** = Kubernetes (keeps time, signals who plays when)
- **Sheet music** = YAML manifests (declares what should run)

Kubernetes ensures the right number of containers are running, replaces failed ones, and routes traffic—just like a conductor keeps the symphony in harmony.

slides.title: Did You Know? 📌
slides.content:
## Kubernetes was born at Google

Google runs billions of containers a week internally with a system called Borg. Kubernetes is its open‑source descendant, now maintained by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF).

slides.title: Kubernetes Features at a Glance ✨
slides.content:
## What makes K8s so powerful?

- **Service Discovery & Load Balancing** – automatically gives each container its own IP and a DNS name
- **Storage Orchestration** – mount local, cloud, or network storage
- **Automated Rollouts & Rollbacks** – update your app without downtime
- **Self‑healing** – restarts failed containers, replaces killed nodes
- **Secret & Config Management** – store passwords, keys, and configs safely
- **Horizontal Scaling** – scale apps up/down with a simple command or automatically

quizData.question: Which of these is a core Kubernetes feature?
quizData.explanation: Kubernetes constantly checks container health and restarts them if they crash.

slides.title: Kubernetes vs. Docker Swarm ⚔️
slides.content:
## Why Kubernetes won the orchestration war

| Feature          | Kubernetes         | Docker Swarm        |
|------------------|--------------------|---------------------|
| **Ecosystem**    | Huge (helm, operators) | Smaller          |
| **Scaling**      | Automatic & manual | Manual only         |
| **Self‑healing** | Built‑in           | Limited             |
| **Complexity**   | Higher             | Simpler             |

Kubernetes is the industry standard today, supported by all major cloud providers.
